import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the Titanic dataset
titanic_data = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Set the style of seaborn
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axis
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# Create a bar plot for survival rate by passenger class and gender
sns.barplot(data=titanic_data, x='pclass', y='survived', hue='sex', ci=None, palette='muted')

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Survival Rate by Passenger Class and Gender', fontsize=14)
plt.xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Survival Rate', fontsize=12)
plt.legend(title='Gender')

# Save the plot
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the Titanic dataset
titanic_data = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Set the style of seaborn
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axis
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# Create a bar plot for survival rate by passenger class and gender
sns.barplot(data=titanic_data, x='pclass', y='survived', hue='sex', ci=None, palette='muted')

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Survival Rate by Passenger Class and Gender', fontsize=14)
plt.xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Survival Rate', fontsize=12)
plt.legend(title='Gender')

# Save the plot
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
